precepts.text: Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins. God hath remembered her iniquities; reward her double according to her works. Come out of the ways and idolatry of America, or receive the same judgment.
precepts.point: I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name, and should ye be utterly unpunished? That is Venezuela, Cuba, IUIC in America, and now US troops heading to Nigeria. The Lord judges us first, and the judgment of the nations follows: a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

precepts.why:
“For, lo, I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name”. That is what you see now: what is happening with Venezuela, with Cuba, with ICE here in America, and now the US sending troops to Nigeria. The Lord is bringing evil upon his people first. “and should ye be utterly unpunished? Ye shall not be unpunished: for I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth”. If the Lord is judging us, understand that the judgment of the nations is soon to come.

But if we do not get rid of the idolatry, the same judgment America gets, we would get. So the voice from heaven says, “Come out of her, my people, that ye be not partakers of her sins, and that ye receive not of her plagues.” Come out of the ways of America. Come out of the idolatry.

“For her sins have reached unto heaven, and God hath remembered her iniquities.” Edom thinks God has forgotten. The Lord remembers every last iniquity, every atrocity, every abomination they have committed. “Reward her even as she rewarded you, and double unto her double according to her works: in the cup which she hath filled fill to her double.”

So if we do not repent of the stubbornness, the bullheadedness and the idolatry, we will get the same judgment. That is why we keep hitting these streets, blitzing, travelling and doing the work of the Lord to wake our people up and bring them out of her.

precepts.text: Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations to drink it.
precepts.point: Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord's hand; the nations have drunken of her wine, therefore the nations are mad.

note.label: America Hedgemony & Oppression

precepts.why:
The Lord told Jeremiah, “Take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations, to whom I send thee, to drink it.” All the nations are made to drink of that cup.

Then Jeremiah 51:7 tells you whose hand the cup is in: “Babylon hath been a golden cup in the Lord’s hand, that made all the earth drunken”. Babylon is America. The Babylon of these days is not just ancient Babylon; it is America. The same cup the Lord told Jeremiah to pour on all the nations is in Babylon's hand, and the Lord is using America, its administration, as his sword to bring judgment on the earth. Whoever sits in office, the next one will take over and it goes on.

That golden cup goes into oppression: falsehood, lies, oppression. “the nations have drunken of her wine; therefore the nations are mad.” What is in the cup is not just riches but America's wrath and ill dealing, like going into Venezuela, taking its president, and then having millions of barrels of oil, about four billion dollars' worth, sent to America as tribute. That is why the nations all over the world are becoming angry with America.

precepts.text: How is Babylon become an astonishment among the nations. That is how we know Sheshach is the United States of America.
precepts.point: The slain of the Lord shall be from one end of the earth to the other. Not lamented, not gathered, not buried; dung upon the ground.

note.label: The Gospel Is Black Liberation

precepts.text: The whole land would be a desolation and these nations serve the king of Babylon seventy years before He punished Babylon; after Babylon we passed to the Persians and Medes, and Cyrus the Persian let us return.
precepts.point: The Most High declares that houses, fields, and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land, because the prophecy was that the captivity would last seventy years and then the people would return.

note.label: Jeremiah 32: Buying the Field of Redemption

precepts.why:
Jeremiah had the evidences put in an earthen vessel “that they may continue many days”, because “Houses and fields and vineyards shall be possessed again in this land.” The evidence had to last because the prophecy was that the captivity would last seventy years and then the people would return.

The Lord had already given the number: “And this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.” The whole land would be a desolation and these nations serve the king of Babylon seventy years before he punished Babylon. After Babylon we passed to the Persians and Medes, and Cyrus the Persian let us return. Then the fields were possessed again, and the sealed and open evidence in the earthen vessel proved whose they were.

precepts.text: The whole land would be a desolation and these nations would serve the king of Babylon seventy years, and only then would the Most High punish Babylon for their iniquity.
precepts.point: The Most High had told through Jeremiah that the people would have to serve Babylon seventy years, but Zedekiah decided to rebel against it instead of submitting to the prophecy.

note.label: Jeremiah 52: The Fall of Jerusalem and the Puppet King Zedekiah

precepts.why:
The Most High had already told through Jeremiah what the people would have to do: “this whole land shall be a desolation, and an astonishment; and these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.” And only when the seventy years were accomplished would he “punish the king of Babylon, and that nation, saith the Lord, for their iniquity, and the land of the Chaldeans, and will make it perpetual desolations.”

Zedekiah decided to rebel against Babylon instead of submitting to the prophecy. He did that which was evil in the eyes of the Most High as Jehoiakim had done, and through the anger of the Most High against Jerusalem and Judah, “Zedekiah rebelled against the king of Babylon.” The seventy years of service had been declared; rebelling against Babylon was rebelling against the word.

moments.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: The Lord told Jeremiah, take the wine cup of this fury at my hand, and cause all the nations to whom I send thee to drink it. So when the Lord says Babylon has been a golden cup in his hand, that cup is going into the Lord's fury. It is going into the fourth seal: America bringing death, famine, and destruction on the earth.

note.label: Beginning of Sorrows & Great Pain

points: And they shall drink, and be moved, and be mad, because of the sword that I will send among them. How did the Lord send the sword amongst all nations back then? He used Babylon. Babylon came and conquered Egypt; Babylon destroyed us; Babylon conquered all those lands. The same way God used ancient Babylon as his cup and as his sword to bring judgment on the whole earth, Mystery Babylon the great holds that golden cup today, and they are bringing forth the fury, death, and destruction on all nations. Their brothers in Europe are going to feel it too.

note.label: Beginning of Sorrows & Great Pain

points: The Lord calls Nebuchadnezzar my servant and sends him against Judah and all the nations round about to utterly destroy them. Nebuchadnezzar is the analogy for Trump: the Lord uses America today to bring judgment on Lebanon, Saudi Arabia and every neighbour of Jerusalem, and the chapter is twofold, ancient Babylon and the last days.

note.label: Trump Is Fulfilling God's Prophecy

points: I begin to bring evil on the city which is called by my name, and should ye be utterly unpunished? That is Venezuela, Cuba, IUIC in America, and now US troops heading to Nigeria. The Lord judges us first, and the judgment of the nations follows: a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth.

note.label: The Iranians & The Ephesians

points: If they refuse to take the cup at thine hand to drink, thus saith the Lord: ye shall certainly drink. God begins to bring evil on the city called by his name, Israel, and should the nations be utterly unpunished? After slavery, lost identity and lost minds for us, the nations are not walking into the kingdom holding our hands.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: I will call for a sword upon all the inhabitants of the earth; prophesy against them, not for them. The Lord shall roar from on high, for he hath a controversy with the nations, the white man, the East Indian, the Arab, the Chinese, and he will give them that are wicked to the sword. The Lord wants you separated from the spirit of America before that judgment.

note.label: There Is No Hate Like Christian Love

points: The wine cup of this fury is a metaphor: go to these nations and prophesy against them whether they accept it or not.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: He sent all His servants the prophets to call every man to turn from his evil way and not go after other gods, promising He would do them no hurt, yet they provoked Him to anger with the works of their own hands.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: Because they would not hear, the Most High will send and take all the families of the north and Nebuchadnezzar the king of Babylon, His servant, against this land to utterly destroy it and make it a perpetual desolation, an astonishment, and a hissing.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: He takes from them the voice of mirth and gladness, the voice of the bridegroom and the bride, the sound of the millstones, and the light of the candle; this is the prophecy that these nations shall serve the king of Babylon seventy years.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: When the seventy years are accomplished, the Most High will punish the king of Babylon and that nation for their iniquity and make the land of the Chaldeans a perpetual desolation.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: Many nations and great kings shall serve themselves of them, and He will recompense them according to their deeds and the works of their own hands.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The Most High gives Jeremiah the wine cup of His fury to make all the nations drink, beginning with Jerusalem and the cities of Judah, so they become a desolation, an astonishment, a hissing, and a curse.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The cup passes to Egypt, the mingled people, Uz, the Philistines, Edom, Moab, Ammon, Tyrus, Zidon, Dedan, Tema, Buz, Arabia, Zimri, Elam, the Medes, all the kingdoms of the world, and last the king of Sheshach.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: They shall drink, be drunken, spew, fall, and rise no more; the Most High is bringing evil first on the city called by His name, and none of the inhabitants of the earth shall go unpunished.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The Most High will roar from on high against all the inhabitants of the earth, for He has a controversy with the nations and will plead with all flesh and give the wicked to the sword.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: Evil shall go forth from nation to nation, a great whirlwind is raised up, and the slain of the Most High shall lie from one end of the earth to the other, unlamented and unburied.

note.label: Jeremiah 25: The Seventy Years Captivity and the Cup of Fury

points: The shepherds and the principal of the flock are told to howl and wallow in ashes, for the days of their slaughter are accomplished; all the wickedness the nations did to us comes back on them, and they drink of the Most High's fury exactly as we did.
